annotations.text:
THE RULE FLIPPED. The previous version of this widget drew video thumbnails and nothing else — no title, no label — on the principle that the agent carries every word and any text in the widget is a worse duplicate of the sentence above it.

That was right for video and is wrong for commerce. A thumbnail is self-explanatory; a purchase isn't. Someone about to spend money needs the product's name and the buy affordance AT THE POINT OF THE TAP, not scrolled up in a paragraph, and no sentence substitutes for a button. So the card now carries: photo, name, the creator's own line, who it's for, and Get it.

The agent's sentence is still not drawn in any artboard — an artboard is a build spec, and anything drawn in one gets built. But the name, blurb and button now MUST be drawn, because they are the component.

TWO COMPONENTS, FOUR CONTAINERS. The old design notes predicted the four view modes would collapse into one responsive strip once the widget was pure thumbnails. Cards pull the other way, but only into two:

DETAIL (1 and 2-3) — photo, name, the creator's line, who it's for, Get it button.
COMPACT (4+ and fullscreen) — photo, name, price. The whole tile is the button.

So src/product-card.ts has one renderProductCard(product, onOpen, detail) and a single IS_DETAIL lookup, not four renderers.

NESTING. Compact tiles are a <button> with aria-label="Get <name>". Detail cards are an <article> containing exactly ONE <button> — the card is deliberately NOT clickable as a whole, because a button inside a button is invalid and breaks keyboard traversal. Tabbing a detail card should stop once.

PLACEHOLDER IMAGERY. The .jpg files here are still 16:9 video stills from the old video-results canvas, standing in for product shots. They are the wrong shape and the wrong subject — real product photography is a centred object, usually on white, which is why .pimg uses object-fit: contain on a neutral ground rather than cover. Swap in real catalog photos before judging spacing or crop.

THE BUTTON GOES OUT. Get it calls app.openLink with a /r/<productId>?q=<questionId> URL — the app's own redirect, which counts the click and then forwards to the merchant. There is no inline browser and no iframe: same stance the video widget took, for the same reason (no cross-host CSP fight).

The redirect never accepts a destination in the request, only a product id it looks up. That's what keeps it from being an open redirect.
